questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: Cushing's syndrome is a.k.a.:
questions.exp: Cushing's syndrome = hypercortisolism (↑↑cortisol), secreted by the zona fasciculata (75% of adrenal cortex). (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: Match cause category — 1) Cushing exogenous (m/c)  2) Cushing inherited defect  3) Pseudocushing … A) Chronic stress of obesity, alcohol, depression  B) Exogenous steroid  C) AME
questions.exp: Cushing: exogenous steroid (m/c), inherited defect AME, acquired ↑cortisol; pseudocushing = chronic stress from obesity, alcohol, depression. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: In the causes table, cortisol (G.C. + M.C.) is inactivated to cortisone (G.C.) by:
questions.exp: Cortisol → cortisone via 11β (OH) steroid dehydrogenase type-2. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: On protein metabolism, hypercortisolism causes:
opts: ↑ protein catabolism with ↓ AA uptake in muscle → proximal muscle myopathy
questions.exp: ↑ protein catabolism, ↓ AA uptake in extrahepatic tissue (muscles), ↓ muscle protein synthesis → proximal muscle myopathy. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: The carbohydrate effect of cortisol is a.k.a. ___.
questions.exp: The carbohydrate arm is a.k.a. adrenal diabetes mellitus: ↑ hepatic AA (alanine) uptake, ↑ gluconeogenesis (alanine >> FFA), ↑ FFA. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: For gluconeogenesis, the preferred substrate order stated is:
questions.exp: Gluconeogenesis uses alanine >> FFA. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: The fat effect of cortisol is best described as:
opts: Fat loss over the trunk with limb obesity
Centripetal obesity with buffalo hump; lipolysis ↑ (minimal)
Uniform whole-body fat gain and lipolysis
questions.exp: Fat redistributes centripetally (buffalo hump) with minimal ↑ lipolysis. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: The mineralocorticoid-action triad of cortisol excess is:
questions.exp: Mineralocorticoid action triad: HTN, metabolic alkalosis, hypokalaemia. (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: The sex-steroid actions listed are acne, hirsutism and, reproductively:
questions.exp: Sex steroid action: acne, hirsutism; reproductive amenorrhoea > oligomenorrhoea (m/c). (Book p844)

questions.sec: Cushing's syndrome: definitions, causes table and metabolic effects · p844
questions.q: The CNS effect of steroid excess described is:
opts: Steroid-induced psychosis, from frank depression to hypomanic depression
questions.exp: CNS effect: steroid-induced psychosis — depression (frank to hypomanic). (Book p844)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: The ocular effects of cortisol excess are:
questions.exp: Eye: ↑ intraocular pressure — cataract and glaucoma. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: Cortisol's anti-inflammatory action is attributed to:
questions.exp: Miscellaneous: ↓ linear growth; inhibits IL-6 → anti-inflammatory action. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: ‘Cortisol excess raises the WBC count yet the patient remains prone to infection.’
questions.exp: Blood/immune: ↑ WBC count but still prone to infection; eosinopenia and ↑ thrombosis (hypercoagulable state). (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: Match the eosinophil clue — 1) Eosinopenia with +ve infection  2) Eosinopenia with −ve infection  3) Eosinophilia … A) Cushing syndrome  B) Addison's disease  C) Typhoid
questions.exp: Eosinopenia with infection → typhoid; eosinopenia without infection → Cushing syndrome; eosinophilia → Addison's disease. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: ACTH-dependent causes account for what share of Cushing's?
questions.exp: ACTH dependent 90%; ACTH independent 10%. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: The single most common endogenous cause overall is:
opts: Ectopic ACTH from squamous cell carcinoma
questions.exp: Pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma (75%), a.k.a. Cushing's disease (micro/macro-adenoma), is the m/c endogenous cause overall. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: The most common paraneoplastic (ectopic ACTH) cause is:
questions.exp: Paraneoplastic tumour (15%): squamous cell carcinoma is m/c; also thymic/bronchial carcinoid, pheochromocytoma/medullary Ca thyroid. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: The m/c cause of Cushing's in toddlers is:
questions.exp: ACTH independent (10%): adrenal adenoma; adrenal carcinoma is the m/c cause in toddlers. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: Match the McCune-Albright (GSα-subunit defect) triad — pick the correct set:
opts: Precocious puberty, café-au-lait spots, lens dislocation
Precocious puberty, fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots
Fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots, atrial myxoma
questions.exp: McCune-Albright triad: precocious puberty, fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots; m/c cause in infancy. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: Primary pigmented nodular adrenal disease (PPNAD) shows ___ and is part of:
opts: Micronodular hyperplasia; Carney's complex (lentigines, atrial myxomas)
questions.exp: PPNAD = micronodular hyperplasia, part of Carney's complex with lentigines and atrial myxomas. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845
questions.q: In adult Cushing's the sex preponderance is:
questions.exp: Adult Cushing's: F > M; diagnosis is made on the discriminatory value of symptoms. (Book p845)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: The proximal myopathy of Cushing's is characteristically:
opts: Bilateral, proximal, symmetric, lower limbs > upper limbs
questions.exp: Proximal myopathy is B/L, proximal, symmetric, LL > UL. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: Facial plethora in Cushing's results from:
opts: Thinning of skin and loss of subcutaneous fat
questions.exp: Facial plethora follows thinning of skin and loss of subcutaneous fat. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: The violaceous striae of Cushing's are due to:
questions.exp: Violaceous striae occur d/t loss of collagen. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: A child with obesity, short stature and delayed bone age presents with fractures. The book links young-onset osteoporosis and fractures to:
questions.exp: Young-onset osteoporosis → fractures, with short stature, obesity and delayed bone age, are important protein-catabolism features. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: Which combination plus central obesity should trigger screening per the Endocrine Society of India?
opts: Protein catabolism features, DM/HTN metabolic syndrome, incidental adrenal mass
questions.exp: Protein catabolism signs, diabetes/HTN metabolic syndrome and incidental adrenal mass + central obesity → screening. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: Match adult vs childhood Cushing's — 1) Adult sex  2) Childhood sex  3) Childhood cause order … A) m >> F  B) Adrenal > pituitary  C) F > M
questions.exp: Adult F > M; childhood m >> F with adrenal > pituitary causes. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: Childhood Cushing's shows LESS of which feature?
questions.exp: Childhood Cushing's: less protein catabolism, obesity, ↑ adrenal androgen → precocious puberty. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: The treatment named for childhood Cushing's with a good response is:
questions.exp: Treatment of childhood Cushing's: radiotherapy (good response). (Book p846)

questions.sec: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first diagnostic cut-offs · p846
questions.q: Cushing's syndrome is ruled out when midnight serum cortisol and midnight salivary cortisol are respectively:
questions.exp: If midnight serum cortisol ≤1.8 µg/dL and midnight salivary cortisol ≤5.5 mmol/L → Cushing's ruled out; otherwise do 8 AM plasma cortisol. (Book p846)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: The EARLIEST finding of endogenous hypercortisolism on the 8 AM plasma cortisol is:
questions.exp: 8 AM plasma cortisol >1.8 µg/dl = loss of diurnal variation, the earliest finding; too low suggests exogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: The over-night dexamethasone suppression test (ONDST) is performed as:
opts: 1 mg oral dexamethasone at 11 pm, then next-day 8 AM plasma cortisol
questions.exp: ONDST: 1 mg oral dexamethasone at 11 pm; next-day 8 AM cortisol <1.8 rules out, >1.8 = endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: On the ONDST, a next-morning cortisol below what value rules out Cushing's?
questions.exp: <1.8 µg/dl rules out Cushing's; >1.8 µg/dl indicates endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: The low-dose DST (0.5 mg Q6H for 2 days) is reserved for:
questions.exp: LDDST is used in suspected pseudocushing, obesity, hyperestrogenism, PCOS or OCP use; >1.8 µg/dl = endogenous hypercortisolism. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: In the ACTH evaluation, a value <10 pg/ml indicates:
questions.exp: ACTH <10 pg/ml = ACTH independent, adrenal cause (10%); >10 pg/ml = ACTH dependent. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: Match ACTH-dependent levels — 1) 10–50 pg/ml  2) 50–100 pg/ml  3) >100 pg/ml … A) Both pituitary & adrenal cause  B) Paraneoplastic syndrome (PNS)  C) Pituitary cause
questions.exp: 10–50 pg/ml pituitary cause; 50–100 both; >100 paraneoplastic (PNS) → PET scan. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: For an ACTH-independent adrenal cause, the imaging step is:
questions.exp: ACTH independent → CT adrenal, showing U/L adenoma or (rarely) B/L hyperplasia. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: After bilateral adrenalectomy, loss of negative feedback risks ↑↑ACTH and an ACTH adenoma known as:
questions.exp: B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy carries the risk of ↑↑ACTH (↓−ve feedback) → ACTH adenoma (Nelson syndrome). (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: Match treatment to lesion — 1) U/L adrenal adenoma  2) B/L hyperplasia  3) Pituitary adenoma (≥6 mm) … A) B/L adrenalectomy  B) Trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy  C) Unilateral adrenalectomy
questions.exp: U/L adenoma → unilateral adrenalectomy; B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy; pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: On MRI brain with gadolinium, a pituitary mass of what size is taken as a pituitary adenoma directly?
questions.exp: ≥6 mm mass → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <6 mm → inferior petrosal sinus sampling; no mass → PET scan. (Book p847)

questions.sec: Diagnostic algorithm: diurnal cortisol, DSTs and ACTH evaluation · p847
questions.q: When MRI shows NO pituitary mass, the next step is:
opts: PET scan; if −ve and high-dose DST +ve go to IPSS, if +ve diagnose PNS
questions.exp: No mass → PET scan: −ve (with high-dose DST +ve) → inferior petrosal sinus sampling; +ve → Dx PNS. (Book p847)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: On inferior petrosal sinus sampling, a petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio above what value is significant for a pituitary adenoma?
questions.exp: Petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio >2:1 (significant) → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <2 → PET scan → PNS. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: A petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio <2 directs the work-up to:
opts: PET scan and a diagnosis of paraneoplastic syndrome
questions.exp: <2 ratio → PET scan → Dx PNS (paraneoplastic syndrome). (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: The high-dose DST regimen and its positive result are:
opts: 2 mg Q6H × 2 days; >50% suppression = pituitary cause
questions.exp: High-dose DST 2 mg Q6H × 2d with >50% suppression indicates a pituitary cause. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: The clinical features of paraneoplastic (ectopic ACTH) syndrome include:
opts: Hyperpigmentation, less protein catabolism, and mineralocorticoid action (HTN, mA, hypokalaemia)
questions.exp: PNS: hyperpigmentation, less protein catabolism, mineralocorticoid action — HTN, mA, hypokalaemia. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: The treatment of choice for Cushing's disease (and relapse-fit patients) is:
questions.exp: Trans-sphenoidal surgery is TOC with a 75% remission rate; radiotherapy is 3rd line if unfit for surgery. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: The remission rate after trans-sphenoidal surgery is:
questions.exp: 75% remission rate after trans-sphenoidal surgery. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: Match the medical therapy — 1) Glucocorticoid receptor inhibitor  2) Adrenolytic in adrenal cancer  3) Prevents relapse (listed first) … A) Mifepristone  B) Mitotane  C) Ketoconazole
questions.exp: Mifepristone = glucocorticoid receptor inhibitor; mitotane = adrenolytic in adrenal cancer; ketoconazole (with pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone) prevents relapse. (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: For patients unfit for surgery, the third-line option is:
questions.exp: If not fit for surgery → radiotherapy (3rd line). (Book p848)

questions.sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848
questions.q: Which drug is NOT listed among the relapse-preventing medical therapies?
questions.exp: Listed: ketoconazole, pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone (II doc), mifepristone, mitotane — not spironolactone. (Book p848)

units.title: Hypercortisolism: definitions, causes and metabolic effects
units.guide: Cushing's = hypercortisolism from zona fasciculata (75% of cortex). Causes: exogenous steroid (m/c), inherited AME, acquired ↑cortisol; pseudocushing = chronic stress of obesity/alcohol/depression. Cortisol (GC+MC)→cortisone (GC) via 11β-HSD2. Effects: protein catabolism → proximal myopathy; carbohydrate (adrenal diabetes) with gluconeogenesis alanine >> FFA; fat redistribution (centripetal, buffalo hump); MC triad HTN+mA+hypokalaemia; sex-steroid acne/hirsutism/amenorrhoea; CNS steroid psychosis.

units.title: Systemic effects, the eosinophil clue and the cause tree
units.guide: Eye ↑IOP/cataract/glaucoma; GI ulceration; ↓ linear growth; IL-6 inhibition (anti-inflammatory); ↑WBC yet infection-prone with eosinopenia and hypercoagulable thrombosis. Eosinopenia +infection → typhoid, −infection → Cushing's; eosinophilia → Addison's. Causes: ACTH-dependent 90% (pituitary adenoma 75% = Cushing's disease = m/c endogenous; paraneoplastic 15% m/c squamous cell carcinoma); ACTH-independent 10% (adenoma; carcinoma m/c in toddlers); others: McCune-Albright (GSα defect; triad precocious puberty/fibrous dysplasia/café-au-lait; m/c infancy) and PPNAD (micronodular, Carney's). Adult F>M.

units.title: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first cut-offs
units.guide: Protein catabolism: B/L proximal symmetric myopathy (LL>UL), facial plethora (thin skin, lost SC fat), bruising, young-onset osteoporosis/fractures with short stature and delayed bone age, violaceous striae (loss of collagen). Plus DM/HTN metabolic syndrome and incidental adrenal mass + central obesity → screen. Childhood: m>>F, adrenal > pituitary, less catabolism, obesity, androgen → precocious puberty; Rx radiotherapy. Rule-out: midnight serum cortisol ≤1.8 µg/dL and salivary ≤5.5 mmol/L.

units.title: The diagnostic algorithm: diurnal rhythm, DSTs and ACTH
units.guide: 8 AM cortisol >1.8 µg/dl (loss of diurnal variation = earliest) → endogenous; too low → exogenous. ONDST 1 mg 11 pm → <1.8 rules out. LDDST 0.5 mg Q6H ×2d for pseudocushing/obesity/PCOS/OCP. ACTH <10 = adrenal (CT adrenal; U/L adenoma → unilateral adrenalectomy; B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy with Nelson risk). ACTH >10: 10–50 pituitary, 50–100 both, >100 PNS (PET). MRI: ≥6 mm → hypophysectomy; <6 mm → IPSS; none → PET.

units.title: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS and medical therapy
units.guide: IPSS petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio >2:1 → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <2 → PET → PNS. High-dose DST 2 mg Q6H ×2d, >50% suppression = pituitary. PNS: hyperpigmentation, less catabolism, MC action. TOC trans-sphenoidal surgery (75% remission); radiotherapy 3rd line; relapse-prevention drugs ketoconazole, pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone, mifepristone (GR inhibitor), mitotane (adrenolytic).
